title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 29-31). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs'. The ingredients are:
- a set M of 'pieces' (cells), ordered by ≤ ('is a face of');
- a set L of 'points', with x ≪ X meaning x lies in the shadow omb(X) of X, and x <° X meaning x lies in the interior omb(X)°;
- a symmetric, irreflexive relation x ∥ y on L (axiom ML0, introduced on p.29), a kind of 'separatedness' or 'distinctness' of points.

From ∥ he defines a compatibility relation on pieces: X ≭ Y iff x ∥ y for all x ∈ omb(X)∖omb(L) and y ∈ omb(Y)∖omb(L). Here omb(L) := ∪_{Z ≤ X,Y} omb(Z) is the shadow of the common faces. Two cells are compatible iff they are separated outside their common faces, like two cells of a polyhedral complex meeting only along shared faces. The stated goal (p.31) is that (M, ≤, ≪, ≭) satisfies the axioms making F, the set of closed (face-closed) subsets of M consisting of pairwise compatible cells, into the expected family of 'complexes'.

This page.

(i) Lemma 3: if X, Y ≤ Z (two faces of one cell), then X ≭ Y. The diagram Z ≥ X, Y ≥ L shows the situation.
- Proof: take x ∈ omb(X)∖omb(L) and y ∈ omb(Y)∖omb(L).
- By ML1 applied to X, Y (faces of a common cell), omb(X)∩omb(Y) = omb(L). Hence x ∉ omb(Y).
- Grothendieck then adds a new axiom, ML4, marked in the margin 'At L 3': if Y ≤ Z, x ∈ omb(Z)∖omb(Y) and y ∈ omb(Y), then x ∥ y. That is, a point of a cell off a face is separated from every point of that face.
- Since x ∈ omb(X) ⊂ omb(Z) and x ∉ omb(Y), ML4 gives x ∥ y.

(ii) Lemma 4: if X ≭ Y, then the conclusion of Lemma 1 holds for X, Y, namely omb(X)° ∩ omb(Y) ≠ ∅ ⇒ X ≤ Y. He notes this uses neither ML4 nor Ax 6.
- Proof: let x <° X and x ≪ Y.
- Compatibility plus irreflexivity of ∥ (ML0) forces omb(X)∩omb(Y) = omb(L). Otherwise some x outside omb(L) would satisfy x ∥ x.
- So there is Z with x ≪ Z ≤ X, Y.
- Since x is interior to X, Z = X. Hence X ≤ Y.

(iii) Lemma 5 (heredity): if X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y and X ≭ Y, then X' ≭ Y'.
- Set-up: take x ∈ omb(X')∖omb(L') and y ∈ omb(Y')∖omb(L'), where L' collects the common faces of X', Y'. Goal: x ∥ y.
- The proof is completed on p.31:
  - If x, y ∉ omb(L), use the hypothesis X ≭ Y.
  - If, say, x ∈ omb(L), use ML1 to get S with x ≪ S ≤ X', Y, so x ≪ Y.
  - Then by ML4 it suffices that x ∉ omb(Y'). If x ∈ omb(Y'), ML1 gives T ≤ S, Y' with x ≪ T. Then T ≤ X', Y', so x ∈ omb(L'), a contradiction.

Purpose: these lemmas show that compatibility behaves like 'meeting properly along common faces'. It implies the frontier/incidence criterion (Lemma 4) and passes to faces (Lemma 5). This is what is needed for face-closed sets of pairwise compatible cells to form complexes.
errors: The machine transcription writes omb(X) ∩ omb(L) in Lemma 3 and Lemma 5; it must be the set difference omb(X)∖omb(L). Otherwise the claim x ∉ omb(Y) would be false, since omb(L) ⊂ omb(Y).
Lemma 3 invokes ML1 to get omb(X)∩omb(Y) = omb(L). This presupposes that ML1 applies to two faces of a common cell Z. That is consistent with the context but not restated here.

Lemma 4 silently uses ML0 (irreflexivity of ∥) to deduce omb(X)∩omb(Y) = omb(L) from X ≭ Y. It also uses the fact that x <° X and x ≪ Z ≤ X force Z = X (the interior/minimality property). Both are legitimate given the earlier axioms; no real gap.
ML4 is introduced ad hoc in mid-proof ('On utilisera alors'), with a margin cross-reference 'At L 3'. The axiom list was still being adjusted as the proofs were written.

ideas.what: Axiomatic calculus of cells with shadows: points ≪ cells, interiors <°, face order ≤, as a combinatorial foundation for 'analysis situs'
ideas.modern_name: Abstract cell complexes / face posets of regular CW or polyhedral complexes; combinatorial models of tame (o-minimal-like) stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abstract cell complexes: Steinitz, Tucker, Kovalevsky. Regular CW face posets: Björner and others. Tame topology programme: Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984), and o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only sketched programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific shadow axiomatics appears unpublished

ideas.what: Compatibility of two cells defined as separation (∥) of their points outside the shadow of their common faces
ideas.modern_name: Cells 'meeting properly' (intersection is a union of common faces), the defining condition of a polyhedral/cell complex

ideas.what: Lemma 3 (faces of one cell are compatible), Lemma 4 (compatibility implies the interior-meets-shadow ⇒ face criterion), Lemma 5 (compatibility is inherited by faces)
ideas.modern_name: Elementary closure properties of cell complexes (subcomplex/face heredity)

missed.claim: Grothendieck is developing a self-contained axiomatics in which complexes are recovered as face-closed families of pairwise compatible cells. The cells come with point-shadows, interiors and a separation relation ∥ on points. The aim is to derive a family F of 'complexes' satisfying his At_M axioms. This 1986 axiomatic route to tame topology appears not to have been published or pursued by others, though this page itself is only routine lemmas within it.
missed.quote: Soit Y ≤ Z, et x ∈ omb(Z)∖omb(Y), y ∈ omb(Y), alors x ∥ y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions, abstract cell complexes in digital topology, and poset models of stratified spaces. It is a primary source for what Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' looked like in practice.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of routine verification lemmas (faces are compatible, a compatibility-implies-incidence criterion, heredity to faces) inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework as a whole is of historical interest, but nothing on this page would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Lemma 3: 'x ∈ omb(X) ∩ omb(L)' should read 'x ∈ omb(X) ∖ omb(L)'. Likewise in Lemma 5: 'x ∈ omb(X')∖omb(L')' and 'y ∈ omb(Y')∖omb(L')'.
ML4 should read: 'Soit Y ≤ Z (X crossed out and replaced by Z), et x ∈ omb(Z) ∖ omb(Y), y ∈ omb(Y), alors x ∥ y'. The insertion '(add Y ≤ Z)' belongs to this, and 'At L 3' is a margin label.
Lemma 4 and Lemma 5 hypotheses: the relation is the compatibility symbol X ≭ Y (as defined on p.29), not 'X ≱ Y'. Likewise the conclusion 'X' ≭ Y''.
Lemma 4: 'X, Y ∈ 𝔐' (the set M of pieces), not '𝒰'.
Margin note reads '(N'utilise pas ML 4, ni Ax_M 6)'.
In Lemma 5 the index set is 'Z ∈ X̌' ∩ Y̌'' (faces common to X' and Y'), as on p.29.
